name: Tayart Tamajeq
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: taya1257 Tayart Tamajeq is not in the catalog. The single swept title, Aikhenvald & Nientao 1988 'On accent in Tamasheq' (Russian, 3-page postgraduate-conference abstract, pp. 3-5, Glottolog 116223), is real (confirmed from Aikhenvald's own CV) but has no digital copy anywhere I could reach: library-print-only, medium priority. In compensation the sweep located and read a first-hand statement for exactly the Niger dialects (tayert/Kel-Fərwan and tawellemmet): Prasse, Alojaly & Mohamed 2003, Dictionnaire touareg-français (Niger), Tome I, 'Note sur l'accent touareg' pp. XX-XXII (archive.org copy saved, pages rendered and read from the image): non-distinctive high-tone weak accent on the enclitic group; penultimate on most singular nouns and internal plurals, antepenultimate on suffixed plurals, vowel-final nouns and simple verb tenses (with leftward shift onto proclitics), final only on a closed exceptional list, fixed morphological accent in intensive tenses. Also saved Prasse 1972 Tahaggart grammar accent section (other variety, pitch-accent with three grades, non-phonological). Not obtained: Kossmann 2011 A Grammar of Ayer Tuareg (high priority, the modern grammar of this exact variety), Louali & Philippson 2005 Faits de Langues 26 doi:10.1163/19589514-02601003 (Brill bot wall, medium). discovery relied on Glottolog, Crossref, archive.org APIs. new_statements.quote: 1) L'accent touareg est un accent dynamique faible et accompagné d'un ton haut, 2) La place de l'accent varie selon la structure de la phrase (l'accent n'a donc pas de rôle distinctif; il n'existe pas de paires minimales de mots distingués par la place de l'accent, sauf par accident absolu), 3) Les groupes enclitiques jouent un grand rôle [...] Accent sur la pénultième. La majorité des noms singuliers, p.ex. akắtab, abắyoy, eyắtem [...] Accent sur l'antépénultième. Les pluriels à désinence. Les pl.1 gardent donc l'accent sur la même syllabe que le singulier. [...] Les temps simples des verbes. On peut dire que les deux temps simples des verbes ont un accent antépénultième latent
new_statements.translation: 1) The Tuareg accent is a weak dynamic accent accompanied by a high tone, 2) The place of the accent varies according to the structure of the phrase (the accent therefore has no distinctive role; there are no minimal pairs of words distinguished by the place of the accent, except by pure accident), 3) Enclitic groups play a large role [...] Accent on the penultimate. The majority of singular nouns, e.g. akắtab, abắyoy, eyắtem [...] Accent on the antepenultimate. Plurals with a suffix. Suffixed plurals thus keep the accent on the same syllable as the singular. [...] The simple tenses of verbs. One can say that the two simple verb tenses have a latent antepenultimate accent
new_statements.citation: Prasse, Karl-G., Ghoubeïd Alojaly & Ghabdouane Mohamed. 2003. Dictionnaire touareg-français (Niger) / Alqamus tamazeq-tafransist, Tome I (A-L). Copenhague: Museum Tusculanum Press, University of Copenhagen. 'Note sur l'accent touareg', pp. XX-XXII.
new_statements.locator: Tome I, front matter 'Note sur l'accent touareg', pp. XX-XXI (quote spans p. XX 'Il n'existe pas...' through p. XXI 'Les temps simples des verbes')
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent (a weak dynamic accent realised as high pitch) is non-contrastive and its position is fixed by morphological category and by the enclitic group, not by syllable weight: most singular nouns (and internal plurals, feminines in -t, noun+possessive groups) are accented on the penult; suffixed plurals keep the accent on the same stem syllable as the singular (so surface antepenult), vowel-final singulars, verbal nouns and the two simple verb tenses take antepenultimate accent (the verb's 'latent' antepenult accent moves onto a preceding satellite or conjunction when possible); a closed set (kălá 'no', wălá 'nothing', numerals 2-10, deictic suffixes, disyllabic interjections, French loans, W plurals that lost -a) has final accent; the intensive perfect and positive intensive imperfect have a fixed stem accent regardless of phrase structure (last stem syllable in conj. I-II-IV, e.g. yəlmâd 'he has learned'; first stem syllable in the intensive imperfect, e.g. yəlámmăd).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Mentioned: suffixed-plural + possessive groups such as iyătemăn-in carry 'un accent secondaire antérieur' (p. XX); and 'Quand la syllabe accentuée est antérieure à l'antépénultième, cette dernière reçoit pourtant un accent secondaire' (p. XXII, e.g. itîkəlăntif, tâbăragăn).
new_statements.exceptions: Final accent in an exceptional closed set (p. XXII): kălá 'non', wălá 'rien', kəllú 'tout' (Arabic), numerals 2-10 (əssín, kărắḍ... mărắw), deictic suffixes -en/-naḍ/-nin/-di, măndám, many disyllabic interjections (kăbắt!), French loans (fărtí, kăntí, mušé, otél), and in tawallammat plurals that lost the ending -a (təfert/šifír). Intensive tenses keep a fixed accent whatever the phrase structure. Weak verbs ending in a vowel accent 'comme s'ils n'avaient pas perdu une syllabe'. The authors open by saying no exhaustive study of Tuareg accent exists.
new_statements.domain_note: The accentual unit is the word or the enclitic group (noun + possessive pronoun, verb + object clitics, preposition + pronoun): with a possessive the accent moves toward the end of the group while remaining penultimate (akătáb-in, akătab-nắsăn); the verb's antepenult accent shifts leftward onto a preceding satellite/conjunction (ád-yəlməd, wər-(y)əlmed, ás yəlmăd). Statement is for the Niger Tuareg of the dictionary (Y = tayart of the Kel-Fərwan, W = eastern tawallammat), with W/Y-specific forms flagged; the authors call it a guide to pronunciation rather than an exhaustive account.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Prasse, Alojaly & Mohamed 2003) is a dictionary of Niger Tuareg based, per its Préface p. V, on two dialects: Y = tayərt of the Kel-Fərwan (Aïr) = Tayart Tamajeq taya1257 [thz] (informant Ghabdouane Mohamed), and W = eastern tawəlləmmət of the Kəl-Əylal = Tawallammat Tamajaq [ttq] (informant Ghoubeïd Alojaly). The 'Note sur l'accent touareg' is written for Tuareg generally with Y/W-specific forms flagged by superscript sigla; a few of its example rows are marked W only. The Tayart-specific grammar (Kossmann 2011, 'Ayer Tuareg') could not be opened. Prasse 1972 on file describes Tahaggart (thv), not this language.

new_statements.quote: 1) L'accent touareg est un accent dynamique faible et accompagné d'un ton haut, 2) La place de l'accent varie selon la structure de la phrase (l'accent n'a donc pas de rôle distinctif; il n'existe pas de paires minimales de mots distingués par la place de l'accent, sauf par accident absolu), 3) Les groupes enclitiques jouent un grand rôle [...] Accent sur la pénultième. La majorité des noms singuliers, p.ex. akátab, abáyoy, eyátem [...] De même, les pluriels 2 (internes) ont l'accent sur la pénultième [...] Accent sur l'antépénultième. Les pluriels à désinence. [...] Les temps simples des verbes. On peut dire que les deux temps simples des verbes ont un accent antépénultième latent
new_statements.translation: 1) The Tuareg accent is a weak dynamic accent accompanied by a high tone, 2) The position of the accent varies according to the structure of the phrase (the accent therefore has no distinctive role; there are no minimal pairs of words distinguished by accent position, except by pure accident), 3) Enclitic groups play a major role [...] Accent on the penultimate. The majority of singular nouns, e.g. akátab, abáyoy, eyátem [...] Likewise the type-2 (internal) plurals have the accent on the penultimate [...] Accent on the antepenultimate. Plurals with a suffix. [...] The simple tenses of verbs. One can say that the two simple verb tenses have a latent antepenultimate accent
new_statements.citation: Prasse, Karl-G., Ghoubeïd Alojaly & Ghabdouane Mohamed. 2003. Dictionnaire touareg-français (Niger) / Alqamus tamazeq-tafransist, Tome I (A-L). Copenhague: Museum Tusculanum Press. ISBN 87-7289-844-5. 'Note sur l'accent touareg', pp. XX-XXII.
new_statements.locator: Tome I, front matter 'Note sur l'accent touareg', pp. XX-XXII (PDF pages 19-21; page renders Prasse2003_TomeI_accent_p-019/020/). Dialect basis: tayert (Y, Kel-Fərwan) and eastern tawellemmet (W, Kəl-Ǝylal), Préface p. V.
new_statements.reading: Niger Tuareg (tayert + tawellemmet) has a non-contrastive, high-tone-marked weak stress computed over the enclitic group. Default placement is penultimate for most singular nouns, internal plurals and noun+possessive groups; antepenultimate for suffixed plurals, vowel-final nouns, verbal nouns, verbal adjectives and the two simple verb tenses (whose accent shifts leftward onto a preceding proclitic/conjunction when available); final accent only on a closed exceptional list (kălá 'no', numerals 2-10, some deictics, interjections, French loans); intensive tenses carry a fixed morphologically determined accent (perfect intensive: last stem syllable in conj. I-II-IV; imperfect intensive: first stem syllable). Morphologically conditioned, mostly penultimate/antepenultimate, not lexically contrastive.

sources.note: Weak dynamic accent with high tone; non-distinctive, position varies with phrase/enclitic-group structure. Penultimate: most singular nouns, internal plurals, feminines in -t, noun+possessive groups. Antepenultimate: suffixed plurals (accent stays on the singular's syllable), vowel-final singulars, verbal nouns, and the two simple verb tenses ('accent antépénultième latent', shifting to a preceding satellite/conjunction). Final: closed exceptional set (kălá, wălá, numerals 2-10, deictic suffixes, interjections, French loans, W plurals that lost -a). Intensive tenses: fixed stem accent. Second…
